question.text: Two blocks rest on a rough horizontal floor, each pulled by a horizontal force F applied to it. Case A: a 4 kg block is pulled by a horizontal force of 20 N; the coefficient of static friction between the block and the floor is 0.6 and the coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.4. Case B: a 2 kg block is pulled by a horizontal force of 20 N; the coefficient of static friction is 0.6 and the coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.4. For each case, determine the block's acceleration and the friction force acting on it.

parts.label: a
parts.asks: Find the acceleration and friction force for the 4 kg block (Case A).

parts.label: b
parts.asks: Find the acceleration and friction force for the 2 kg block (Case B).

conditions: force is applied horizontally to a block on a horizontal rough floor
μs = 0.6 and μk = 0.4 in both cases
applied force F = 20 N in both cases

figure.description: Two separate cases, each a single block sitting on a horizontal rough floor. A horizontal force F pulls the block to the right (arrow drawn pointing right from the block). Case A: block mass 4 kg, F = 20 N, μs = 0.6, μk = 0.4. Case B: block mass 2 kg, F = 20 N, μs = 0.6, μk = 0.4.

solution.approach: In each case compare F to the maximum static friction; if F is smaller the block stays still and friction matches F, otherwise the block slides and kinetic friction applies.

steps.text: Case (a): find the maximum static friction the 4 kg block can have.
Compare this to the applied force. Since F = 20 N is less than 24 N, the block does not move, and friction equals F.
Case (b): find the maximum static friction the 2 kg block can have.
Compare this to the applied force. Since F = 20 N exceeds 12 N, the block slides, so kinetic friction acts instead.
Apply Newton's second law to the sliding block using kinetic friction.

final_answer.value: (a) block stays still: acceleration = 0, friction = 20 N. (b) block slides: acceleration = 6 m/s², friction = 8 N (kinetic).

common_mistakes.text: Assuming case (a) also slides and using kinetic friction anyway, giving f = 16 N and a = 1 m/s² instead of the correct rest state.
Using the static maximum 12 N as the friction force in case (b) instead of the kinetic value 8 N, giving a = 4 m/s² instead of 6 m/s².
